statements.quoted: House passes bill from @RepStutzman and @RepBillFoster to give financial agencies a technology boost https://t.co/dV8YXO6VKL via @MattBracken

statements.text:
There is important work to be done in Washington, but Speaker Johnson sent everyone home until after the election. 

I've joined my colleagues in calling on Johnson to bring Members of Congress back to Washington so we can get to work on AI. https://t.co/AF9lq3aFEz

AI is advancing at a concerning pace, and Congress needs to act. Meanwhile, President Trump wants to sit on his hands and "leave it exactly where it is."
 
He had the opportunity to make progress with China this week on global AI cooperation, but he is more interested in protecting Big Tech billionaires than safeguarding Americans from potentially dangerous technology. 

https://t.co/zGVaH86fYX

“Morally binding” agreements like this aren’t going to cut it when AI agents continuously code better versions of themselves that could evade human oversight. 

Congress must get off the sidelines and pass meaningful, technically feasible AI guardrails. https://t.co/rCkjpgvI7w
statements.quoted: President Trump touted a "morally binding" agreement with AI executives to "self-police" and floated a “committee” of roughly 10 people to help “watch over the whole enterprise” https://t.co/xY8qUBqdZe https://t.co/63NdrIpTQn

statements.text:
AI is giving Americans new options to manage their money. AI tools that chase higher interest rates may benefit savers—and this will have sweeping implications for our financial system. 

Read my @WSJ op-ed with former Congressman @JohnDelaney on how AI could affect your bank or credit union:

https://t.co/X6RMIVYfJl
We need to encourage stronger ID verification tools to combat deepfake scams. @PeteSessions and I already have a bipartisan bill that would help states roll out these tools: https://t.co/kxDYx49HPL

AI agents are making it easier for bots and crooks to impersonate you online and gain access to your accounts. Congress and regulators must step up their game to harden our financial system against these vulnerabilities. https://t.co/xNKpbbFCZx
statements.quoted: SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents operating inside customer accounts, with some agents attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions. https://t.co/QGmAmvmtEK

statements.text:
When we get back to DC, we need to hit the ground running on protecting Americans and our financial system against AI risk. 

Unlike Republican leadership, with @RepJeffries, we will finally have a Speaker who understands Congress needs to get off the sidelines.

It was a pleasure to attend and speak at The Open Source in Finance Forum (OSFF) New York 2026 hosted by the Fintech Open Source Foundation.

I spoke about how technology like AI can make our financial system more efficient, promote stability, and protect consumers. As Congress begins a new session, we must prioritize the safety of our financial system and support responsible innovation.

Congress has the tools to prevent powerful AI chips from getting in the wrong hands and posing a national security risk. 

My bipartisan, bicameral Chip Security Act with @RepHuizenga would help stop chip smuggling and has already passed unanimously out of committee in the House. 

It's time to get it across the finish line.

statements.text: “With advances in AI creating new cybersecurity threats and financial risks, it’s more important than ever that we modernize the way we monitor the health of our financial institutions,” [...] “We cannot afford to rely on outdated systems to oversee an increasingly complex financial sector.”
